key_insight: Microscopic residual impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films are degradation nucleation sites, and can be rapidly identified with microscopy-plus-ML before devices fail.
engineering_relevance: The work provides a fast, non-invasive screening tool to quality-check perovskite layers and improve stability control for scalable solar-cell manufacturing.
method: nano-FTIR, high-resolution optical microscopy, and scanning probe techniques to chemically validate impurity regions
High-resolution reflected-light microscopy with machine learning image analysis for rapid impurity detection
Photo-stress and degradation tracking to link impurity density with early failure
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that impurity-rich films degraded faster in early stages, and that the imaging framework could detect and quantify harmful impurities within seconds.
watch_item: Performance may depend on calibration to specific film chemistries and imaging conditions, so transferability across perovskite formulations should be verified.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
